newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March spot natgas prices notionally unchanged.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March spot natgas prices notionally unchanged.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for March were notionally steady Thursday as most nomination deadlines had expired for first-of-the-month deliveries, sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast swing prices for March were talked unchanged in the mid-$1.70s, still sharply lower than February indices in the $2.80s.
February prices for Friday delivery were also mostly steady in the mid-$1.80s, except on Transco (Station 65), where prices gained about five cents to the low-to-mid $1.90s.
In the Permian basin, March gas prices were talked in the high-$1.50s to low-$1.60s, up about two cents from Wednesday's levels but still about $1 under February indices.
Permian prices for Friday delivery were mostly in the low-$1.80s.
Southern California border prices for March were notionally in the high-$1.50s, while Feb prices were talked in the high-$1.80s.
In the Midcontinent, March prices remained in the mid-$1.60s, though swing Demarcation prices were talked in the low-$1.70s.
February prices in the Midcontinent slipped a few cents into the low-to-mid $1.70s, with Demarcation quoted at $1.80.
In the East, New York city-gate prices for March were talked around $2.15, down about $1.45 from February indices.
American Gas Association reported Wednesday that gas stocks as of last week were at 33 percent of capacity at 1,064 bcf. Stocks fell 63 bcf from the previous week.
